paper_metadata.title: Topological phase inversion after long-term thermal exposure of nickel-base superalloys: Experiment and phase-field simulation

evidence.quote: The evolution of the microstructure has been quantified in the second generation single crystal Ni-base superalloy ERBO/1, which belongs to the family of CMSX-4, submitted to long-term aging at 1100 °C for up to 250 h.

through formation of interfacial dislocation networks in the g/g0-interfaces the g-channels are no longer stabilized by the elastic energy induced by coherency stresses and strains and therefore the g0-particles are able to coalesce [30]
